claim: Systems Manager provides public parameters for public AMIs maintained by AWS; when you launch instances with a public parameter, such as one under /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest, you use the latest AMI, because the parameter always points to the latest AMI version in the Region.
question: How can an instance launch always use the latest Amazon Linux AMI without hard-coding its AMI ID?

values.display: public parameters for public AMIs maintained by AWS
always points to the latest version

qualifiers.scope: per public AMI parameter, per Region

evidence.quote: AWS Systems Manager provides public parameters for public AMIs maintained by AWS. You can use the public parameters when launching instances to ensure that you're using the latest AMIs.

For example, the public parameter `/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64` is available in all Regions and always points to the latest version of the Amazon Linux 2023 AMI for arm64 architecture in a given Region.
